Release validation checks

Focused CLI, provider and desktop checks required before publishing a GateFox release.

About 9 min read · 17 sections

On this page

These are the detailed checks for step 4 of the release workflow.

Run real model tool loops against the installed command on the test Mac. Use isolated native and gateway state directories. Record configuration digests, provider registration, client-requested chat names, and resume results.

SSH proxy transport

For SSH proxy changes, run scripts/e2e-ssh-proxy.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --codex SIGNED_NATIVE_CLI --root FRESH_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It uses the real native byte proxy, a real WebSocket upgrade, and an isolated Unix listener to verify that device identification precedes the initialize request only inside the upgraded session. No account or provider inference is used.

Subagent routing and payloads

For gateway sub-agent routing, run scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --code CHECKOUT --root FRESH_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. Repeat with --private, --openai, --cold --mixed-identity, and --cold --config-override. The real SDK spawns a child against a local mock provider, opens it using the desktop's resume shapes, and continues it while checking its saved identity and reasoning. These checks use private homes and no paid inference. --baseline reproduces the pre-fix alias rejection. Add --v2 to verify that the delegated task and a follow-up reach the child, that it executes a real command, and that its history includes that command and the resulting answer. --v2 --expect-payload-loss reproduces the missing-task failure in 0.5.1.

Live collaboration transport

Before shipping collaboration transport changes, also run scripts/e2e-subagent-live.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --code CHECKOUT --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY_CONFIG --model CONFIGURED_CODEX_ALIAS --root FRESH_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. This opt-in check uses real subscription inference and isolated chat homes. It requires an actual child command and an answer containing a proof available only in the child's read-only fixture file.

Chat lists and disconnected execution

For chat-list status changes, run scripts/e2e-chat-state.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --root FRESH_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY, then repeat with --native and a second evidence directory. Repeat with --private for per-connection gateway executors. Two clients of the real SDK must expose an already-running chat and receive its actual idle event without resuming it or starting another inference. The fixture uses a local mock provider and private state. By default it checks the checkout's compiled adapter with the package's verified SDK; pass --code INSTALLED_PACKAGE to check the packaged adapter too. These checks do not prove the phone's unread rendering. For Gateway-owned execution reporting, also run the fixture with --activity. Require the same running turn, a saved completion and a provider failure after both application clients disconnect, with no repeated inference or native configuration changes. Verify the Gateway Activity screen separately; neither this fixture nor this screen establishes Codex unread-dot behavior.

Shared execution

For shared execution changes, run scripts/e2e-shared-execution.mjs with the installed command, isolated native home, and isolated client configuration. Start without --inference, then enable real provider turns and image history. The zero-inference run proves process ownership rather than durable chat resume. Every host it starts, including the restart phase's replacement, is stopped at the end, and a detached reaper (scripts/e2e-reaper.mjs) cleans up after a SIGKILL of the check: its process groups, the SDK sockets its links name that nothing serves (with their .lock files) and its private home. It kills only groups it saw alive: a group that emptied or answers no probe is never signalled again, so a reused process ID cannot be hit. The check starts its host from the dist of an installed package: pass --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE, or leave it out and the script uses the package that --gateway's launcher runs (its current/package). Only when neither has dist/execution-host.js and dist/config.js does it fall back to the checkout's ../dist, and a package that ships gateway-sdk then refuses with "requires a matching installed gateway SDK". The first JSON line printed names the dist used, so confirm it is the installed package. Give the isolated native home a fixture models.json named by model_catalog_json, as the other end-to-end scripts do, and start the SDK once on it before the check, so the two adapters do not run the first catalog preflight at the same moment.

Speed controls

For speed controls, run scripts/e2e-fast-mode.mjs --gateway INSTALLED_COMMAND --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --root PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It uses the real signed SDK with a mock upstream through stdio and a private Unix socket. It proves requested and returned tiers, settings changes, saved-history resume, and native isolation; it sends no subscription inference and does not prove rendered desktop controls or the built-in cloud transport.

Named worker context

For named Qwen role context changes, run scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --code CHECKOUT --root TASK_DIRECTORY --v2 --role-fork --named-worker --cold. Repeat in a fresh directory with --worker-stale-catalog --worker-compact. Require the actual named Qwen child to report its bounded context, retain its model and effort, execute tools, resume after the cold host restart and compact exactly once in the second run. These checks use synthetic inference and do not spend provider credit.

Chat Completions translation

For Chat Completions translation changes (local Qwen or another chat-completions-api provider), run scripts/e2e-chat-compaction.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY_CONFIG [--provider qwen]. It sends the compaction shape (no tools, tool_choice, an undeclared historical tool), a turn with declared tools and an undeclared historical tool, and an oversized prompt to the real provider, and requires an answer, an answer, and context_length_exceeded. 1.2.2 fails all three. It prints only PASS/FAIL lines and fixed error codes. When the model's metadata lists image input, or with --vision, it also sends a user image and a tool-result image and requires the model to name their colors. For Chat Completions failure handling, run E2E_ROOT=FRESH_DIRECTORY node scripts/e2e-chat-tool-retry.mjs LABEL GATEWAY_COMMAND. A real Codex client must retry a garbled tool call and finish. It uses a local mock and spends no credit.

Chat identity

For chat identity changes, run scripts/e2e-identity.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --root PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. With the package's own gateway SDK and a mock upstream it proves that new chats are recorded as gatefox by default (a chat saved as subscription_gateway before 1.8.0 keeps its id), and that with the openai opt-in a new gateway chat is recorded as openai (thread, rollout and SQLite), is in the registry when its start returns, compacts locally on the selected model, routes to the gateway when a new connection resumes it, sends nothing with the gateway token to the ChatGPT backend, and is listed by a default thread/list; and that a legacy chat stays subscription_gateway and is listed through the router but not by a stock engine.

Compaction and recovery

For compaction changes, run scripts/e2e-compaction-switch.mjs --gateway INSTALLED_COMMAND --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --root PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY --expect selected-turn --shared. This is the release step. A package that ships gateway-sdk (0.4.3 and later) compacts inside the user turn, so the run verifies the package's own gateway SDK receipt and selected-model recovery, Stop, failures, and reconnect through stdio and Unix with a mock upstream and the signed SDK. The script detects gateway-sdk in the package (through its dist/gateway-sdk-runtime.js, else the same file layout). When the package has it, selected-turn is the default and automatic and baseline are refused; when it does not, selected-turn is refused. --expect automatic and --expect baseline are for legacy packages without gateway-sdk only (baseline reproduces the previous-model failure of the stock SDK). --codex does not change the SDK of the gateway executor, which always runs the package's own gateway-sdk; it only replaces the SDK the script itself starts and checks. The script uses gateway-sdk/gateway-codex in the package and says so if it is missing. Every child runs under a private HOME inside the run folder, so no execution host home or receipt reaches ~/.local/state. Only the pinned SDK's fixed socket folder, /tmp/codex-daemon-UID, stays outside, because the SDK hard-codes it; the script removes its own stale sockets there. A passing run removes its /tmp/gw-compact-switch-* run folder; a failing run keeps it, and --keep-fixture keeps it on request. With --shared, the selected-turn run also checks the shared execution host over stdio; a legacy automatic run only checks the safe refusal of automatic compaction, not seamless recovery.

Managed worker context

For managed worker context changes, also run scripts/e2e-managed-routing.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --code CHECKOUT --root FRESH_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It uses the verified bundled SDK with a mock provider to prove compaction exceeds the ordinary byte budget within its bounded recovery allowance, preserves a proof from the original history, and resumes an ordinary turn below the original limit. It uses private state and no paid inference.

Responses continuation

For Responses continuation changes, run scripts/e2e-responses-continuation.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --codex SIGNED_CODEX_MACH_O --root FRESH_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It verifies actual continuation flags, message phases, nested text, and one dispatched tool with the pinned signed SDK and a mock upstream. Pass the signed Mach-O under CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex, not its unsigned bin/codex shell launcher. The fixture requires fresh isolated state, rejects native homes, and uses no copied authentication or paid inference.

Interrupted Responses terminals

For interrupted Responses terminals and missing-terminal recovery, run scripts/e2e-responses-terminals.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE --codex SIGNED_CODEX_MACH_O --root FRESH_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It verifies the original acknowledged SDK turn, actual incomplete terminals, minimal completed terminals, once-only tool execution, safe pre-output EOF retries, and partial-output failure. It uses localhost mocks and isolated state, with no native authentication or paid inference.

Reasoning levels

For reasoning levels, run scripts/e2e-reasoning-levels.mjs with the same --gateway, --config, --codex and --catalog options plus a fresh --fixture and --output. Pass the native model cache (~/.codex/models_cache.json) as --catalog, never the gateway catalog, or gateway aliases are routed as native models. It checks Max and Ultra on Claude Opus and Codex Sol: the effort Codex sends, Ultra's collaboration tools, and, for Claude, the CLI's actual --effort and --thinking-display flags.

Goals and model changes

For goal durability, run scripts/e2e-goal-outage.mjs with the same options. It starts an active goal on a gateway model, SIGKILLs the adapter and every SDK child mid-turn like a power cut, then resumes and requires the goal to survive and finish. Both use real inference in an isolated native home. For model switches during a goal, run scripts/e2e-goal-switch.mjs with the same options. It starts an active goal on --from, switches the chat to --to with thread/settings/update as the picker does, and requires the next turn to start by itself and send its requests on the new model. It also uses real inference in an isolated native home. A first real turn is required before the SDK can resume an empty chat.

Execution sandbox

Run scripts/e2e-execution-sandbox.mjs to confirm the live control socket is unreachable inside the actual macOS sandbox, including through its alias.

Native resume and forks

For native resume, fork or reasoning changes, run scripts/e2e-native-model.mjs --gateway INSTALLED_COMMAND --root FRESH_PRIVATE_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY. It sends the desktop's own resume and fork shapes after an engine restart to the signed SDK directly and through the adapter, and requires the adapter to give each the same model and effort. It uses isolated homes and a localhost mock upstream, with no authentication or paid inference.
